extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, academics, students, advocacy partners, and potential funders
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational description of the Institute for Policy Integrity: its mission, history, areas of work (research and advocacy), team and governance, funding practices, and educational/partnership activities. The page communicates standards and practices the organization follows in producing policy research and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-partisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute for Policy Integrity is a non-partisan think tank dedicated to improving the quality of governmental decisionmaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes non-partisan stance as foundational to work; research and advocacy are presented as oriented toward improving decisionmaking rather than partisan goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce original scholarly research
rubrics_metrics.description: We produce original scholarly research in the fields of economics, law, and public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work includes reports and academic articles; research output is scholarly in nature and intended to contribute to academic and policy conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary substantive focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Our primary area of focus is environmental and energy policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities and research prioritize environmental and energy topics, with an emphasis on protecting the environment and public health through expanded cost-benefit analysis and economically sound policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of economic analysis to inform policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim of expanding cost-benefit analysis to protect the environment and public health and to identify and support a wide range of economically sound policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places economic arguments at the center of policy advocacy and research; seeks to apply rigorous economics to regulatory issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy through legal and administrative channels
rubrics_metrics.description: We engage in federal and state policy advocacy, frequently submitting amicus briefs, public comments, and expert testimony in court cases and legal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy methods explicitly include formal legal filings (amicus briefs), agency engagement (public comments), and expert testimony; these are presented as standard avenues for influencing policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with advocacy organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: We regularly collaborate with advocacy organizations, offering legal and economic expertise to advance shared policy goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships with groups such as Environmental Defense Fund, Sierra Club, and Union of Concerned Scientists are highlighted as mechanisms for combining expertise and advancing policy objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical education and student training
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the NYU School of Law, we lead the Regulatory Policy Clinic, which offers students practical experience in administrative law and policy analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization provides hands-on experiential learning for students, integrating clinic work with the Institute’s research and advocacy activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff and advisory expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff and fellows provide in-depth legal and economic analysis on climate, energy, and other regulatory issues; the Institute relies on the guidance and support of an advisory board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights qualifications of staff/fellows and the role of a prominent advisory board in guiding work; implies standards for staff expertise and governance oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding transparency and source restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants from philanthropic foundations provide the vast majority of our funding. We have not accepted any funding from corporations or corporate foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares funding sources and a policy of not accepting corporate or corporate foundation funding as a credibility and independence practice; lists example foundations that have supported the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic integrity and authorship practices
rubrics_metrics.description: All of our work is fully aligned with NYU’s academic integrity policies, and we are the sole authors of our research publications and advocacy materials except where co-authors are expressly acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts adherence to institutional academic integrity standards and transparent authorship: work is internally generated and co-authorship is explicitly acknowledged when present.
